summary: The GNOME desktop layer for a Fedora 44 bootc image, targeting GNOME 50 (gnome-shell 50.3, mutter 50.3, gnome-control-center 50.3, gdm 50.1). It provides the Wayland-only GNOME session, GDM greeter, Settings/settings-daemon, Nautilus plus its gvfs/thumbnailer/search backends, the GNOME portal backend, a curated core app set, tweaking/extension tooling, and colour-management stack. Fedora 44 ships GNOME as Wayland-only — there is no gnome-session-xsession and no /usr/share/xsessions/gnome-xorg.desktop, so there is no X11 fallback session to bake. On the group question: @workstation-product-environment is the wrong tool here — comps shows it is an environment composed of base-graphical, container-management, core, desktop-accessibility, firefox, fonts, gnome-desktop, guest-desktop-agents, hardware-support, libreoffice, multimedia, networkmanager-submodules, printing and workstation-product, i.e. it drags in Firefox, LibreOffice, printing, fonts, codecs and container tooling that this project's desktop-common layer already owns. @gnome-desktop is the correct group, but its default (non-mandatory) member list pulls gnome-boxes (full libvirt/qemu), rygel, gnome-remote-desktop, sane/hplip scanner backends and the NetworkManager VPN plugins. A dry-run resolve measured 145 packages for the full group vs 62 for `dnf install --setopt=group_package_types=mandatory @gnome-desktop`. Recommendation: use an explicit package list (below), or the mandatory-only group plus explicit additions, never the bare group and never the environment.

integration.detail: Enable the greeter and graphical boot in the Containerfile: `systemctl enable gdm.service` and `systemctl set-default graphical.target`. gdm.service is the only system unit gdm ships (plus gnome-headless-session@.service).

PRIMARY dconf-baking mechanism for bootc: gschema overrides. Write /usr/share/glib-2.0/schemas/50-<yourorg>.gschema.override then run `glib-compile-schemas /usr/share/glib-2.0/schemas/` as the last step of the RUN layer. This lives entirely in /usr, so it is image-managed, atomically replaced on upgrade, and cannot drift. Fedora itself uses exactly this pattern — see the shipped 10_org.gnome.desktop.background.fedora.gschema.override and org.gnome.software-fedora.gschema.override.

SECONDARY mechanism, for the two things overrides cannot do: locking keys, and setting relocatable-schema paths (e.g. org.gnome.settings-daemon.plugins.media-keys.custom-keybinding:/…/custom0/). Use /etc/dconf/db/local.d/00-<name> keyfiles plus /etc/dconf/db/local.d/locks/<name>, then `dconf update`. The dconf package already ships /etc/dconf/profile/user containing `user-db:user` + `system-db:local` + `site` + `distro`, so no profile authoring is needed. CAVEAT: this writes the binary db into /etc, which bootc 3-way-merges across upgrades — a stale machine-local /etc/dconf/db/local can shadow your intent. Keep /etc usage minimal and confined to locks.

GDM greeter settings are a separate dconf profile: /usr/share/dconf/profile/gdm reads /etc/dconf/db/gdm.d. Put greeter tweaks (banner message, disable user list, greeter scaling/night-light) in /etc/dconf/db/gdm.d/ and run `dconf update`. gdm also ships /usr/share/gdm/greeter-dconf-defaults as the read-only default set.

/etc/gdm/custom.conf for autologin (AutomaticLoginEnable/AutomaticLogin), TimedLogin, and — if you ever need it — WaylandEnable. On F44 setting WaylandEnable=false leaves GDM with no session to launch, since no X11 GNOME session exists. Do not ship that.

Bake default-application choices in /usr/share/applications/gnome-mimeapps.list, not mimeapps.list. GNOME's XDG_CURRENT_DESKTOP=GNOME causes the desktop-prefixed file to be consulted first, and it lives in /usr so it is image-managed. Run `update-desktop-database /usr/share/applications` afterwards.

colord ships /usr/lib/udev/rules.d/69-cd-sensors.rules (colorimeter/spectrophotometer uaccess tagging — i1Display, ColorMunki, Spyder, huey) and 95-cd-devices.rules (display/scanner/camera device enumeration). Installing the colord RPM is sufficient; no custom rules needed. If you use an unlisted or newer instrument, add a drop-in in /usr/lib/udev/rules.d/ with TAG+="uaccess" — this is exactly the kind of thing that justifies baking rather than post-install scripting.

colord.service and colord-session.service (user) are D-Bus activated — do NOT `systemctl enable` them. Same for the gsd-* user units. What you may want to enable is org.gnome.SettingsDaemon.Color.target's presence, which comes from gnome-settings-daemon automatically.

power-profiles-daemon.service, switcheroo-control.service and iio-sensor-proxy.service ship enable presets. Verify with `systemctl preset-all` semantics in your build; on a minimal fedora-bootc base presets are usually applied, but assert them explicitly if the Settings power panel matters.

gnome-remote-desktop ships gnome-remote-desktop.service + gnome-remote-desktop-configuration.service (system, for headless/login-screen RDP) and three user units. Leave all disabled unless remote access is an intentional feature of the image — a group-default RDP listener on every machine is a real attack surface.

NVIDIA + Wayland: ensure nvidia-drm.modeset=1 (and on 555+ nvidia_drm.fbdev=1) is on the kernel command line. RPM Fusion's akmod-nvidia usually drops this in modprobe.d, but on a bootc image with a baked initramfs it is safer to also set it as a kernel arg in the bootc/bootupd config. This belongs to the GPU layer, but the GNOME layer is what breaks (black screen, no session) when it is missing.

COLOUR MANAGEMENT, medical imaging: the pipeline is colord (device+ICC database) -> gsd Color plugin -> GPU gamma LUT. Verified in mutter 50.3: the compositor applies only the VCGT/gamma ramp from the profile. It does NOT perform a display-referred colour transform of application output. Any app that needs true colour-managed rendering must do its own lcms2 transform and fetch the profile from colord itself. Ship colord + colord-extra-profiles + argyllcms + DisplayCAL and treat per-application CMS as an application-layer requirement, not something the DE provides.

COLOUR MANAGEMENT, HDR: mutter 50.3 has real HDR plumbing — verified symbols meta_kms_update_set_hdr_metadata, meta_set_drm_hdr_metadata, HDR_OUTPUT_METADATA, supported-color-modes, bt2100 handling, and a new org.gnome.mutter output-luminance gsettings key (a(ssssud): connector, vendor, product, serial, colour mode, luminance). This is a BT.2100/PQ signalling path, not an ICC pipeline. Do not conflate it with diagnostic colour accuracy.

FRACTIONAL SCALING: verified against /usr/share/glib-2.0/schemas/org.gnome.mutter.gschema.xml on F44 — org.gnome.mutter experimental-features now documents ONLY 'kms-modifiers' and 'autoclose-xwayland'. Both 'scale-monitor-framebuffer' and 'xwayland-native-scaling' have graduated and are unconditionally active. Do NOT ship the old override experimental-features=['scale-monitor-framebuffer']; it is a no-op on F44 and is pure cargo cult. Fractional scale is a first-class Settings > Displays control, and Xwayland apps now scale natively rather than being blurrily upscaled. For diagnostic imaging displays, still prefer 100% or 200% integer scale to guarantee 1:1 pixel mapping — fractional scale means the compositor resamples, which is unacceptable for pixel-accurate DICOM review.

VRR: fully implemented in mutter 50.3 and no longer experimental. Verified symbols meta_kms_update_set_vrr, meta_output_is_vrr_enabled, the 'refresh-rate-mode' property, and the runtime warning 'Output is VRR capable, but a possible CRTC for the output does not support VRR'. It is a per-monitor toggle in Settings > Displays. Important for baking: the setting is stored in the user's ~/.config/monitors.xml as a refresh-rate-mode of 'variable', NOT in dconf — so it cannot be set via gschema override or the dconf db. You can only pre-seed it per-user via /etc/skel/.config/monitors.xml (fragile, monitor-serial specific) or leave it to the user. The greeter's own copy lives at /var/lib/gdm/.config/monitors.xml.

TEARING: not supported. A full symbol scan of libmutter-18.so.0 found zero tearing/immediate-flip/tearing-control-v1 symbols. GNOME does not implement wp_tearing_control_v1 and offers no 'allow tearing' or unredirect-for-fullscreen tearing mode. For the gaming purpose, VRR is the only latency mitigation available in-session; if tear-free-off / immediate presentation is a hard requirement, the escape hatch is running the game inside gamescope (which does implement it) — that belongs in the gaming layer, not here.
No custom groups required. colord runs under its own system user created by the RPM; colorimeter access is granted by uaccess tagging rather than plugdev membership, so do not add users to plugdev.

risks: @workstation-product-environment is the wrong choice and will duplicate/conflict with the desktop-common layer: comps shows it composes base-graphical, container-management, core, desktop-accessibility, firefox, fonts, gnome-desktop, guest-desktop-agents, hardware-support, libreoffice, multimedia, networkmanager-submodules, printing and workstation-product. It brings Firefox, LibreOffice, CUPS/printing, fonts and codecs — all of which desktop-common owns.

Bare `dnf install @gnome-desktop` resolves 145 packages because comps 'default' members are installed alongside 'mandatory'. That silently pulls gnome-boxes (entire libvirt+qemu stack), rygel (a DLNA/UPnP media server listening on the LAN), gnome-remote-desktop, sane-backends-drivers-scanners, libsane-hpaio, and seven NetworkManager VPN plugins. Measured: 145 packages full vs 62 with --setopt=group_package_types=mandatory. Prefer the explicit list above.

webkitgtk6.0 is ~92 MiB installed and is dragged in by yelp, gnome-initial-setup and gnome-online-accounts. It is both the single biggest contributor to layer size and a large CVE surface that you now must rebuild the image to patch. Dropping yelp + gnome-user-docs is the only meaningful lever, at the cost of F1 help.

gnome-software on bootc: gnome-software-rpm-ostree understands rpm-ostree-managed systems, but a pure bootc image updated via bootc-fetch-apply-updates.timer is not the same thing. Expect gnome-software to either show nothing useful or offer a misleading OS update path. Recommended mitigation: ship a gschema override on org.gnome.software disabling the packagekit/rpm-ostree plugins and let it manage Flatpaks only, with bootc owning OS updates.

gnome-initial-setup runs on first login and will interrupt a pre-provisioned image. It is gated on ~/.config/gnome-initial-setup-done, so either drop the package, or seed that marker via /etc/skel. It is a mandatory member of @gnome-desktop, so a group-based install brings it back.

Fedora 44 has no X11 GNOME session at all — verified, gnome-session ships only wayland-sessions/gnome.desktop. Any workload that genuinely needs Xorg (some proprietary medical viewers, older CAD, certain NVIDIA configurations, screen-capture tools that predate PipeWire portals) has no in-session fallback. This is the single highest-impact constraint of choosing GNOME on F44 for this project.

Unpackaged extensions from extensions.gnome.org break at every GNOME major bump (50 -> 51). Baking them into /usr/share/gnome-shell/extensions/ at build time means a shell that fails to load extensions after the next Fedora rebase, with no user-level recovery on an immutable host. Restrict baked extensions to the Fedora-packaged ones (which get rebuilt per release) and let users add the rest at runtime.
gnome-tweaks is 49.0 against a 50.3 shell. It mostly works but is drifting; some panels are already redundant with Settings. Do not build workflows or documentation that depend on it.

Shell themes via gnome-shell-extension-user-theme are explicitly unsupported by upstream GNOME and break on minor updates. Fine to include the extension; do not ship a custom shell theme as the default.

gnome-color-manager is 3.36.2 — a GTK3 app that has seen essentially no upstream development in years, while colord itself is 1.4.8 and healthy. The calibration UX is dated and it is plausible Fedora drops the frontend in a future release. For medical imaging, treat DisplayCAL/ArgyllCMS as the real tool and gnome-color-manager as the Settings-panel shim.

Fractional scaling plus a colour-critical display is a genuine conflict: fractional scale means compositor resampling of app output. Combined with the fact that mutter only applies the VCGT and not a full colour transform, a fractionally-scaled diagnostic display gives neither pixel accuracy nor colour accuracy. Document 100%/200% as the supported configuration for imaging workstations.

VRR state cannot be pre-configured from the image because it lives in per-user ~/.config/monitors.xml keyed by monitor serial, not dconf. Any 'VRR on by default' requirement will need a first-login script or per-machine provisioning, which partly defeats the point of baking.

gnome-remote-desktop is a comps default member and ships a system service. If it slips in via a group install and gets enabled by preset, every machine from the image exposes an RDP surface. Explicitly assert it disabled, or omit the package.
copr: (none required) — every package listed under `packages` resolves from fedora/updates or RPM Fusion. No COPR is needed for a complete GNOME 50 layer on F44. Flagging this explicitly so nobody adds one speculatively: COPRs are the main source of upgrade breakage on atomic images, since a COPR that has not rebuilt for F45 will block the rebase.
flatpaks: com.mattjakeman.ExtensionManager — Extension Manager. Not packaged in Fedora and the canonical delivery is Flathub. Also the right call on an immutable host: it browses/installs extensions into ~/.local/share/gnome-shell/extensions, which is user-writable, so it works without touching the image.
org.gnome.Boxes — prefer over the gnome-boxes RPM. The RPM drags the whole libvirt/qemu/edk2 stack into the image for a feature most users never touch; the Flatpak bundles its own qemu.

io.github.realmazharhussain.GdmSettings — GDM Settings. Only useful if you want interactive greeter tweaking; for a baked image, /etc/dconf/db/gdm.d is the correct mechanism and this is just a discovery aid.
org.gnome.design.Palette and org.gnome.Snapshot-style GNOME Circle apps generally — for anything outside the core set, prefer Flathub over RPM so app churn does not force image rebuilds.
com.mattjakeman.ExtensionManager is the only one of these that is genuinely load-bearing; the rest are preferences.

external.name: Unpackaged GNOME Shell extensions (DING/desktop-icons-ng, ArcMenu, Vitals, Tiling Assistant, OpenWeather)
external.method: If they must be baked: download the .shell-extension.zip from extensions.gnome.org at build time, unzip into /usr/share/gnome-shell/extensions/<uuid>/, run `glib-compile-schemas` on any bundled schemas dir, and enable via a gschema override on org.gnome.shell enabled-extensions. Strongly discouraged — these break on every GNOME major and you cannot fix them without a rebuild. Preferred method is runtime install by the user via gnome-browser-connector or the Extension Manager Flatpak.

external.name: Custom ICC display profiles for calibrated imaging workstations
external.method: Not an RPM. Drop vendor/measured .icc files into /usr/share/color/icc/ at build time so they are image-managed, then bind them to devices at runtime with `colormgr device-add-profile`. Per-device binding is inherently machine-local (keyed by monitor serial) and cannot be fully baked.

external.name: None otherwise
external.method: No upstream RPM URLs or installer scripts are required for this layer.

services: gdm.service — enable. The one unit that must be enabled for this layer to do anything.
colord.service — D-Bus activated, do NOT enable.
colord-session.service (user) — D-Bus activated, do NOT enable.
power-profiles-daemon.service — preset-enabled; assert explicitly if the Settings power panel matters.
switcheroo-control.service — preset-enabled; needed for 'Launch using Discrete Graphics Card'.
iio-sensor-proxy.service — preset-enabled; needed for auto-rotate and ambient-light brightness.
gnome-remote-desktop.service — leave DISABLED unless remote access is an intentional feature.
gnome-headless-session@.service — template unit from gdm; not enabled directly.
org.gnome.SettingsDaemon.*.service (user units from gnome-settings-daemon) — started by the gnome-session targets, never enabled manually.
size_note: A dry-run of the recommended explicit set (94 packages resolved) reported ~137 MiB download / ~430 MiB installed on a host that already had most GTK/Qt/Mesa libraries present, so that figure badly understates a bare quay.io/fedora/fedora-bootc base. Realistic incremental cost on a minimal bootc base is roughly 1.5–2.0 GiB. For calibration, `@gnome-desktop` full resolves to 145 packages and `--setopt=group_package_types=mandatory @gnome-desktop` to 62. Measured install sizes of the dominant items: webkitgtk6.0 ~92 MiB (pulled by yelp/GOA/initial-setup), mesa-dri-drivers ~52 MiB (though that belongs to desktop-common), gnome-backgrounds ~38 MiB, gnome-control-center ~24 MiB, appstream-data ~14 MiB, gnome-shell ~14 MiB, gnome-software ~12 MiB, mutter ~9 MiB. The rest is GTK4/libadwaita, GStreamer, LLVM (via Mesa), and the app set. Cheapest meaningful reductions, in order: drop yelp + gnome-user-docs (kills webkitgtk6.0, ~92 MiB), drop gnome-backgrounds if shipping custom wallpapers (~38 MiB), drop gnome-boxes/rygel/scanner backends by not using the bare group (already excluded above).
notes: Deliberately excluded as desktop-common territory, per the brief: fonts (incl. adobe-source-code-pro-fonts and the fonts group), PipeWire/WirePlumber, flatpak, podman/toolbox, CUPS/printing, GStreamer codec packs, mesa-dri-drivers and mesa-vulkan-drivers (these come from comps group base-graphical, along with plymouth-system-theme), avahi, glib-networking, NetworkManager and its VPN plugins, PackageKit, and the base xdg-desktop-portal package. Note that base-graphical is exactly three packages — mesa-dri-drivers, mesa-vulkan-drivers, plymouth-system-theme — so desktop-common should own it explicitly rather than relying on GNOME to pull it.

Judgement call flagged for the parent: xdg-desktop-portal-gtk is listed here rather than in desktop-common. It is technically GTK-generic (Cinnamon/Budgie/Xfce also want it), but on GNOME it is the required fallback for portal interfaces xdg-desktop-portal-gnome does not implement. If desktop-common already ships it, drop it from this layer.

Second judgement call: the accessibility trio (orca, at-spi2-core, speech-dispatcher) comes from the desktop-accessibility comps group, which also contains brltty. at-spi2-core is arguably DE-agnostic infrastructure; orca is specifically GNOME's screen reader. Consider moving at-spi2-core to desktop-common and keeping orca here.

adw-gtk3-theme, qt6-qtwayland-adwaita-decoration and qadwaitadecorations-qt5 are listed here because their entire purpose is making non-GTK4 apps match GNOME. If the project also ships a KDE layer, these will conflict aesthetically — they are harmless but pointless there, so keep them GNOME-scoped.

Recommended Containerfile shape for this layer: a single RUN that does `dnf -y install <explicit list>` (or `dnf -y install --setopt=group_package_types=mandatory @gnome-desktop <extras>`), then writes the gschema override, then `glib-compile-schemas /usr/share/glib-2.0/schemas/`, then `update-desktop-database /usr/share/applications`, then `systemctl enable gdm.service && systemctl set-default graphical.target`, then `dnf clean all`. Consider --no-docs to shave the layer; it costs man pages, which on an immutable host you may not want to lose.

Open question for the parent: is gnome-software wanted at all? On a bootc image where the OS is updated by bootc and apps by Flatpak, its value is a Flathub GUI. If desktop-common already provides a Flatpak store front-end, gnome-software + gnome-software-rpm-ostree + appstream-data could be dropped entirely (~30 MiB plus PackageKit).

Open question: does the medical-imaging purpose need a specific GNOME configuration profile (locked 100% scale, night-light disabled, a fixed colour profile), and if so should it be a separate dconf-locks drop-in layered on top of this one? The locks mechanism (/etc/dconf/db/local.d/locks) is the right tool and belongs in the purpose layer, not here.

Open question: the gaming purpose will likely want VRR on by default, which — as established — is not bakeable via dconf. Somebody needs to decide whether a first-login script seeding ~/.config/monitors.xml is acceptable, or whether the gaming workstations get a different DE where tearing control also exists.

Verification method used, for reproducibility: all package names were confirmed by batched `dnf repoquery --qf '%{name}\n' <names…>` on a live Fedora 44 host with fedora, updates and RPM Fusion free/nonfree enabled; only names echoed back are listed under `packages`. Group composition came from `dnf group info` plus direct parsing of the comps-Everything.x86_64.xml from the repo cache (dnf5 has no `environment` subcommand, so the environment definition was read from comps directly). VRR/tearing/scaling claims were verified against the installed mutter 50.3 gschema XML and a symbol scan of /usr/lib64/libmutter-18.so.0, not from memory.
